title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
content:
# Abstract

Large language models explore general knowledge stored implicitly in their parameters. However, their ability to access and precisely manipulate knowledge is still limited, and they often hallucinate. We explore general-purpose fine-tuning recipes for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) models which combine pre-trained parametric and non-parametric memory for language generation. We introduce RAG models where the parametric memory is a pre-trained seq2seq model and the non-parametric memory is a dense vector index of Wikipedia, accessed with a pre-trained neural retriever (DPR). We compare two RAG formulations: one that conditions on the same retrieved passages across the whole generated sequence, and another that can use different passages per token. We evaluate our models on a wide range of knowledge-intensive NLP benchmarks, showing state-of-the-art results on Natural Questions, WebQuestions, and CuratedTREC, and generate more specific, diverse, and factual language than parametric-only seq2seq baselines.

title: GraphRAG: Unlocking LLM Discovery on Complex Datasets
content:
# Abstract

The use of retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to retrieve relevant information from an external knowledge source has emerged as an indispensable paradigm for extending LLM capabilities. However, existing RAG approaches struggle when queries require holistic comprehension of an entire corpus or global multi-hop reasoning connecting diverse entities. To address this limitation, we present GraphRAG, a modular pipeline combining knowledge graph generation, community detection hierarchy, and LLM-assisted summarization. By constructing an entity-relationship graph from the raw text corpus and generating multi-level modular community summaries, GraphRAG enables global question answering that significantly outperforms naive RAG on broad thematic discovery and comprehensive multi-hop query evaluation.
